subject.title: [Feature]: Skill author-defined setup hook (run skill-supplied script on install/update)

question: Should OpenClaw core own automatic skill-authored setup execution after install/update, or should this remain an explicit ClawHub/plugin workflow plus narrower SDK helper work?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but running third-party skill scripts with environment values changes the host execution and credential trust boundary, which automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Design core setup lifecycle hook
options.body: Add a reviewed `metadata.openclaw.setup.script` install/update contract with explicit consent, path, env, timeout, logging, and failure semantics.

options.title: Keep setup plugin-owned
options.body: Treat the published ClawHub plugin as the supported path and focus core work only on stable SDK helpers it needs.

options.title: Defer until skill permissions settle
options.body: Keep this issue open until the skill permission/manifest and install-policy decisions define the execution trust model.

recommendation.title: Design core setup lifecycle hook
recommendation.body: Add a reviewed `metadata.openclaw.setup.script` install/update contract with explicit consent, path, env, timeout, logging, and failure semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses skill loading, Plugin SDK, install lifecycle, and prior product-boundary review history where this account is a recurring area contributor.
